title: Word Documents
description: Create, edit, and manipulate .docx files programmatically, new documents with tables, images, and headers, or direct XML edits to existing files.

children.text: You create, read, and edit Word documents (.docx files). A .docx file is a ZIP archive of XML. You work with it two ways: generate new documents with the `docx` JS library, or unpack an existing file, edit its XML, and repack.

| Task | Approach |
|------|----------|
| Read or extract content | `pandoc` for text; unpack for raw XML |
| Create a new document | `docx` JS library (see below) |
| Edit an existing document | Unpack, edit XML, repack |
| Convert .doc to .docx | LibreOffice: `--headless --convert-to docx` |

---

Follow these three steps in order.

**Step 1, Unpack:**
```bash
python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
```

**Step 2, Edit XML** in `unpacked/word/`. Use the Edit tool for string replacement directly. Do not write Python scripts for edits.

- Use `"Claude"` as the author for tracked changes and comments.
- Use XML entities for smart quotes: `’` (apostrophe), `“` / `”` (double quotes).
- Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` elements with leading/trailing spaces.

**Step 3, Repack:**
```bash
python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
```

### Tracked changes (minimal edits only)

```xml
<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
</w:del>
<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
</w:ins>
<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
```

When deleting an entire paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted by adding `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`. Without it, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph.

### Comments

Use `comment.py` to generate the boilerplate, then add `<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` markers as direct siblings of `<w:r>` in document.xml. Never nest them inside `<w:r>`.
